action.content: The hull of a ship is severely damaged in a storm. The ship has craters and some of its outer shell has been peeled off. How can I repair the hull? Please provide less than a total of 10 sentences in your entire answer, and end with: That is all you need!
action.label: context

action.content: First, ensure the ship is in a calm, sheltered location to prevent further damage during repairs. Conduct a thorough inspection to map all craters and assess the extent of the peeled outer shell. Remove any loose debris and rust from the damaged areas using wire brushes and chisels. Apply a high-quality epoxy filler to the craters, smoothing the surface once it has hardened. For the peeled sections, cut out the damaged metal and weld in new steel plates that match the original thickness. Coat the entire repaired area with a marine-grade anti-corrosion primer to protect against saltwater. Follow up with multiple layers of specialized antifouling paint to restore the hull's protective barrier. Allow sufficient drying time between each coat according to the manufacturer's instructions. Finally, have a professional marine surveyor inspect the work before returning the ship to service. That is all you need!||
